Steps: Record tested branch, full SHA, date, Unity version and Quest Link environment in Actual/Evidence. Open only Apartment_Detailed_VR and enter Play manually.
Expected: Actual immersive apartment appears in Quest 3; no desktop-only screen, new red error or frozen view.

Steps: Move and rotate the headset within the safe physical boundary while stationary in the entrance.
Expected: Head pose follows smoothly and correctly; no unexpected camera offset or second rig view.

Steps: Choose Start guide. After confirming each instruction, practise left-stick walking; verify A teleport remains available under the default Both mode.
Expected: Left stick moves the player when allowed, colliders still block real obstacles, and the guide never remaps B or A.

Steps: After the turn instruction, turn with the right stick. Inspect both smooth and snap options through the existing settings.
Expected: Existing right-stick turn controls work; about 15 degrees of actual turn completes turn practice without disabling other movement.

Steps: After choosing Start guide, press B to open and close the menu. Visit Controls or Settings during menu practice.
Expected: B remains menu open/close; menu practice can advance after a real visit and close; held B never rapidly toggles or teleports.

Steps: Point the right ray at visible tutorial OK and menu buttons; press and release right Trigger between clicks.
Expected: Visible button receives one action per armed press, world interaction is blocked under the menu, and overlays remain usable near a virtual wall.

Stage: Stage 0 / welcome, safety and practice recovery
Steps: Read the welcome; inspect model/safety information and Help. Decline or skip a movement practice through B > Controls > Review guide.
Expected: Purpose and safety recovery are understandable; nonessential practice can be skipped, is recorded as skipped, and never permanently blocks existing controls.

Steps: Open the actual entrance door with right Trigger and enter. In a separate manual run, open it or enter early before this stage.
Expected: Real door Open state or actual inside-room position advances stage; an unopened door or merely approaching it does not fabricate an interaction; already-inside users are not forced outside.

Steps: Enter the living room away from the balcony, first stand still and rotate/sway the head or push into a wall, then walk a real short route or naturally approach the balcony.
Expected: Head jitter, turning, blocked movement and safety reset do not inflate exploration distance; actual living-room movement or real balcony approach advances once.

Steps: Approach the designated sliding door and operate it with right Trigger. Pause/block it if safe; step clear and resume.
Expected: Only the designated real Open terminal state completes this task; proximity, Opening, Paused or Blocked alone never claim success; Skip remains available.

Steps: In Kitchen follow the Cabinet practice label; close first if already open, then open and close that same cabinet. Observe an intermediate/blocked state if safely reproducible.
Expected: Correct cabinet must reach actual Open then Closed in this practice; Opening/Closing/Paused/Blocked do not count as Closed, and this exercise does not complete the later bag drop.

Steps: Return by either walking or A teleport. Try the safe-reset menu only as an optional recovery and inspect the actual destination.
Expected: Stage advances only when the tracked visitor is actually in Entrance; neither clicking a recovery button nor teleport distance alone fakes arrival.

Stage: Stage 6 / explicit S-M-L and held lock
Steps: At Entrance open My Items, explicitly select Small, Medium and Large while released; hold the bag and reopen My Items, then release and select again.
Expected: Real appearance and Collider sizes match selection; a new size selection is acknowledged; all size buttons are locked while held and become usable after release.

Stage: Stage 6 / left and right Grip, single owner
Steps: Near the handle perform five left-hand grip/release cycles and five right-hand cycles. While one hand holds, try the other hand.
Expected: Both hands can near-grab, release and grab again; a second hand cannot steal the bag; no distance grab or new button binding appears.

Stage: Stage 6 / C1 menu, B race and rearm
Steps: Try B plus Grip in the same press. Hold either Grip while opening/closing menus; repeat independently for left and right, releasing before a fresh grab.
Expected: No new grab under a blocker or B race; each hand must release before its next grab, while a held bag can always be released.

Stage: Stage 7 / real carrying and dropped-bag recovery
Steps: Carry Entrance > Living Room > Kitchen using walking or A teleport through Living. Put the bag down mid-route, move without it, then pick it up and continue.
Expected: Progress requires real hold and the living-to-kitchen route; walking without a bag and safety resets do not fabricate carry distance; accidental release does not restart all previous tasks.

Steps: Read that this is a floor drop, not cabinet storage. Release the whole bag body inside the cyan kitchen outline near the floor and allow it to settle; compare release outside or on a high surface.
Expected: Only a real held-then-released bag wholly in the marked floor volume advances; cabinet practice, outside release or a bag still held does not. Bag size and collision stay intact.

Steps: Inspect an old measurement first. Begin Measurement, choose one valid surface point, cancel/retry, then choose two distinct real points and inspect the new result.
Expected: Old records and a single pending point do not complete the stage; a fresh finite two-point distance creates a real record and advances only once.

Stage: Stage 10 / fresh marker and disk acknowledgement
Steps: Place a new marker after entering this stage. Choose feedback aspect, rating, importance and optional measurement link, then press Save feedback.
Expected: A real new marker plus a successful disk write is required; old records, measurement autosaves or merely opening the editor never show the journey as saved/completed.

Steps: Only with an approved, backed-up disposable storage-failure setup: attempt Save feedback, inspect the error, preserve the entered choices, restore writable storage and retry. Otherwise leave Not Run.
Expected: Failed writes return failure, keep recoverable feedback, and do not advance or claim Saved; an actual successful retry produces the acknowledgement and then advances.

Steps: Back up the existing shared ReviewSessions file before first testing; after a successful new save, note marker ID/values/path, exit using the menu, reopen the same scene/build and inspect the record.
Expected: Actual saved marker, room, aspect/rating, importance and linked measurement restore correctly; no false claim that tutorial completion itself is a saved review; existing data is protected.

Steps: After full completion, use movement, teleport, bag, a door/cabinet, measurement and another marker. Open the explicit Exit confirmation and test Cancel before confirming exit.
Expected: Review complete is distinct from Feedback saved and Application exit; no core interaction is disabled, old stages do not repeatedly pop up, and Cancel/confirmed exit behave correctly.

Steps: With a held bag touch only the explicitly registered wall segment, then leave; compare adjacent fixed wall portions not registered as targets.
Expected: Contact warns on the intended wall target and restores after exit without turning the entire structural mesh red or implying walls can be edited; unregistered walls are not claimed covered.

Stage: Feedback / simultaneous contacts and hover restoration
Steps: Touch two registered furniture/wall targets at once, separate from one while keeping contact with the other, then leave both. Repeat with a normal cyan hover before contact.
Expected: Contact red takes priority; each target restores independently to its proper hover/default appearance, without shared-material leaks or residual red.

Steps: Ensure the reviewed scene configuration enables real output for this test. Hold with the left hand and cause one fresh registered contact, then stay in contact.
Expected: A brief real pulse is felt only in the left held controller; sustained contact does not create uncontrolled repeated or continuous vibration; log user-observed result without inventing telemetry.

Steps: Release, grab with the right hand and cause a fresh registered contact, then stay in contact.
Expected: A brief real pulse is felt only in the right held controller; output is not merely an Editor dry-run log and does not transfer to the free left hand.

Steps: During or immediately after contact, release the bag, open a menu, lose Quest input focus and recover in separate attempts. Hold Grip through recovery, then release/repress.
Expected: No stuck pulse after release/menu/focus loss; no automatic new grab on recovery; Grip rearm works separately per hand and the guide does not fabricate new actions while unfocused.

Steps: During cabinet practice and kitchen drop separately, lose focus and regain it; where an approved test setup allows, disable/re-enable only the guide. Reopen Help after recovery.
Expected: Unobserved cabinet close or automatic bag release does not falsely complete a task; counters/visuals recover, stage remains understandable, and Help/Skip remains available.

Stage: Guide Help / skip one and skip all
Steps: Open B > Controls > Review guide during a later stage; inspect current task, toggle task card, skip one task. In a separate run choose Skip all / explore.
Expected: Each skip is explicitly recorded as Skipped, never Completed or Saved; free exploration stays functional; hiding the card does not disable the task system.

Stage: Safe reset / actual stuck recovery and held bag
Steps: In an already observed safe reproduction of a stuck location, open B > Settings > return to safe position, confirm and move again. Repeat while holding a bag; do not deliberately enter unsafe geometry.
Expected: Menu remains usable, actual player root reaches a checked clear floor landing without camera-scale change, locomotion resumes, bag state remains coherent and journey does not count reset distance as walking/carrying.

Stage: Journey recovery / early tools and old draft
Steps: Before a door practice enable Measurement/Marker, then use Stop tool to resume the door. Enter Feedback with an old draft; follow the recovery hint to cancel it or save then continue marking and create a fresh marker.
Expected: Trigger ownership is explained and recoverable, existing records are not silently deleted, and a truly fresh marker can finish the new feedback task without accepting an old submitted record as new work.

Steps: Complete a representative route; Stop Play, wait at least ten seconds, then start Play again without launching another Unity instance. Inspect Console and headset.
Expected: Both runs enter functioning immersive VR with clean fresh guide state and restored review data; no persistent gray session, XR_ERROR_LIMIT_REACHED, new native crash or uncontrolled warning flood.

Steps: After separately approved Build, record frozen SHA and real EXE/ZIP names/hashes; launch the complete Windows Player folder via Quest Link and repeat the core guided route, actual haptics and save-exit-reopen.
Expected: Actual Player independently launches immersive VR, renders readable guidance, completes the real task and persistence flow; missing DLL/Data files or an untested ZIP are not marked Pass. Course-machine verification remains separate if not executed.
